appraisal_events.evidence: "il vit bien le salut et le rendit, mais sans s'arrêter ; et, s'éloignant à toute vitesse, sans un sourire, sans qu'un muscle de sa physionomie bougeât, il se contenta de tenir pendant deux minutes sa main levée au bord de son képi, comme il eût répondu à un soldat qu'il n'eût pas connu"; the narrator then runs to the barracks, "où on ne me laissa pas rester", and cannot say goodbye.
appraisal_events.explanation: Driving past with another friend, Saint-Loup answers his friend's greeting with the impersonal salute owed to an unknown ranker; the narrative reports the treatment flatly and lets its coldness stand without comment.

status_effects.explanation: He is the one who needs and signals — the large greeting, the run to the barracks, the desolation at missing the farewell — while Saint-Loup gives nothing and drives on.
He is left on the far side of every threshold in turn: not taken up into the tilbury, treated as a stranger rather than an intimate, then turned out of the courtyard where the regiment is forming.

ambiguities: Whether Saint-Loup's passing salute is a deliberate cut is left open: the narrator supplies his short-sightedness and the presence of a companion, so the same gesture reads either as a snub or as an accident of military form.
